subject: ORD function
notes: Re-verified independently and it survives, including the edge that killed r1. Class national arrived with COBOL-2002, so r2 applies 2002+. The national table is SPARSE over the full 65,536 code units (AlphabetBindNationalLiteralPhrase: no & 0xFF mask, no fixed-size array) and NationalCollation.Weight computes an unspecified code unit's position as NextFree + (c − |specified codes below c|) — the §12.3.7 GR7 k3 arithmetic, which is correct under ALSO collapsing. PROBED: ALPHABET RN FOR NATIONAL IS N"A" ALSO N"B" with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL IS RN printed ORD(N"A")=00001, ORD(N"B")=00001, ORD(N"C")=00067 — all three match the hand-derived GR7 k3 values, and 00067 is exactly the case the alphanumeric r1 path gets wrong. Routing: BindIntrinsicCore sets CollateNat (never the alphanumeric Collate) whenever the argument's category is National, so the 256-entry alphanumeric table can never alias a national character; with no ALPHABET … FOR NATIONAL literal phrase in effect the identity body Ord(string) IS the r2 value (D-N3 code-unit order). Premise checks that killed two candidate findings: a NATIONAL GROUP item — the one shape whose category OperandCategory returns null for — is unreachable because GROUP-USAGE appears in no grammar rule and is explicitly not modelled; and a class-national-but-category-national-edited argument (PIC NBN), which would route to the alphanumeric weights, is loud-rejected at bind with COBOL0899 before ORD ever sees it. Both test-refs exist and pin ORD VALUES on the national path (char_national ORD=19991 on the native sequence; alphabet_national ORD-A=00003 and ORD-SP=00036 under a REV-NAT literal phrase).
